info.title: Epovest API
info.summary: Measure how AI assistants answer the questions your market asks, and shape those answers.
info.description:
Epovest is an AI visibility platform: it measures how AI assistants such as ChatGPT, Claude,
Gemini, Perplexity, Mistral and Grok answer the questions a market asks (which names they cite,
with which sources, how that changes over time), and gives businesses the levers to shape those
answers and get recommended.

Every call carries an API key in the `Authorization` header: `Authorization: Bearer epo_...`.
Keys belong to an Epovest account and are created by its owner in the app. Scopes are chosen at
creation: `read`, which every key has, and `write`, for creating and changing things. Each
operation of this document states the scope it takes under `x-scope`.

The same surface is served as MCP tools at `https://mcp.epovest.com/mcp`, one tool per route:
each operation names its tool under `x-mcp-tool`. The prose reference of both surfaces is at
https://epovest.com/docs/api.md, and the task recipes at https://epovest.com/docs/recipes.md.

The canonical base URL is `https://api.epovest.com/v1`. The base delivered earlier,
`https://app.epovest.com/api/v1`, answers identically.

Rate limit: 120 requests per minute per credential, sliding window. Beyond the budget the API
answers `429 rate_limited` with a `Retry-After` header and the `X-RateLimit-Limit` and
`X-RateLimit-Remaining` counters. MCP calls draw from the same budget.

Conventions: dates are ISO 8601 with timezone, survey periods are plain `YYYY-MM-DD` dates,
enumerations use their lowercase value, monetary amounts are integers in minor units suffixed
`_minor` next to a `currency` field, errors always use the envelope
`{"error": "slug", "message": "human sentence"}`, and paginated routes answer with `pagination`
as `{page, per_page, total, pages}` where `page` is clamped rather than rejected: ask for page 99
of 3 and you get page 3 back, so stop on `pagination.page >= pagination.pages`.
info.x-brand-owner: Epovest is a brand operated by Sels de Rehy, LLC, a limited liability company incorporated in the State of Delaware, United States.

get.summary: List the trackers of the account
get.description:
The trackers of the account, current versions, the ones still followed first and then the
ones filed away.

parameters.name: project
parameters.description: A project UUID, or `default` for the trackers filed under no project.

200.description: The trackers of the account.

404.description: The `project` filter names no project of the account.

post.summary: Create a tracker, in draft
post.description:
Creates a tracker in draft: it measures nothing until started. Starting it launches its first
survey immediately, unless it carries a chosen `next_survey_at` still in the future, in which
case the grid starts on that date. That first survey runs on every frequency, `on_demand`
included, where it is also the last one until `POST /trackers/{id}/survey` asks for another.
Manager or above.

get.summary: Read one tracker
get.description:
One tracker, by id. A retired version still answers here with `status: "retired"`, so after an
edit that made a new version, follow the new id rather than the one you had cached.

200.description: The tracker.

patch.summary: Update the configuration of a tracker
patch.description:
Takes the same fields as the creation, all optional: only the fields you send change, and a
sent list replaces the previous one entirely. Keywords, analysts and the title apply in
place. Changing the prompts, engines, frequency or resolution of a version that HAS measured
creates a new version: the score series continues across versions, and the response carries
the new tracker with its new id, next to `version_created`. A version that has not measured
yet is amended in place and keeps its id, so `version_created` is `false`.

A paused tracker takes all of it, the collection settings included. The call writes the
configuration and nothing else: no survey runs, no credit is reserved, the tracker stays
paused with its `pause_reason`, and what you set takes effect at the next
`POST /trackers/{id}/start`. A version created this way is born paused as well. Manager or
above.

200.description: The tracker as it now stands, and whether a version was created.

version_created.description: True when the edit recorded a new tracker version, which carries a new id.

409.description: `not_editable`: a retired version is revision history and takes nothing.

post.summary: Start or restart the measurement
post.description:
Starts the measurement against the credit balance, and its first survey runs there and then,
whatever the frequency, unless a chosen `next_survey_at` is still in the future: with one set,
nothing runs until that moment, and that holds for a date chosen while the tracker was paused.
Restarting a paused tracker picks its schedule back up, at whatever configuration it carries
now. Replaying it on a tracker already measuring answers with that tracker. Owner only.

200.description: The tracker, measuring.

409.description:
`tracker_archived`: bring it back first with `POST /trackers/{id}/archive` and
`{"archived": false}`. `not_startable`: a retired version never restarts, work on the
current version instead.

post.summary: Run one survey now, on top of the schedule
post.description:
Runs one survey NOW: the anchor, the frequency and the date of the next scheduled survey are
untouched. Answers `201` with the survey, which carries `on_demand: true` and `requested_at`;
its point joins the series under the same period, told apart by `on_demand`. On a tracker
whose frequency is `on_demand`, this is where every survey after the first one comes from.
Debits the balance like any survey. While one is still running, answers `200` with THAT
survey.
A refusal never pauses the tracker: the schedule asked for nothing and keeps running.
Owner only.

201.description: The survey that was just started.

200.description: A survey of this tracker was already running: it is the one that comes back.

409.description:
The refusal names the move that unblocks: `tracker_not_active` (start it first),
`tracker_archived` (bring it back first), `already_starting` (another call is starting
one right now, nothing spent).

post.summary: Pause the measurement
post.description:
Pauses the measurement; the series is kept. Recorded as a `manual` pause, which a top-up
leaves as it is: it waits for `POST /trackers/{id}/start`. Owner only.

200.description: The tracker, paused.

409.description: `not_active`: only an active tracker can be paused.

post.summary: File a tracker away, or bring it back
post.description:
The body is the STATE you want: omitted it files the tracker away, `{"archived": false}`
brings it back, and both moves answer the same when replayed. A tracker still measuring
pauses in the same call, so the answer carries `status: "paused"` to say it. The sheet and
the score series are kept. Owner only.

200.description: The tracker, filed away or back to the list.

422.description: `invalid_tracker`: `archived` must be a boolean.

get.summary: List the surveys of the tracker chain
get.description:
The surveys of the tracker chain, newest first. `panel_version` is the tracker version that
ran each one (the series spans versions), and `billed_analysts` lists the AI analysts
reserved on that survey, what the credit hold covered.

200.description: The surveys of the chain.

get.summary: Read the score series
get.description: The score series, one row per analyst, keyword, engine, version and period.

parameters.name: analyst
parameters.description:
One of the analysts that carry a score. The `custom_prompt` analyst yields a text note
per response, so it is read through `GET /trackers/{id}/responses`.

200.description: The score series.

get.summary: Read the raw answers of one engine
get.description:
The answers that succeeded, in surveys that completed. Each one carries the text the engine
wrote, the sources it cited, `uncited_sources`, the pages it read to write the answer, and
`searched`, whether it went to the web (`null` when undetermined, for answers measured before
the field existed).

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Keeps the answers whose text carries this wording.

parameters.name: question
parameters.description: Keeps the answers to this question.

parameters.name: survey
parameters.description: A survey id of this chain.

parameters.name: tone
parameters.description:
The answers where the sentiment analyst judged a keyword mention with that tone, so a
week's negative answers come back in one call.

parameters.name: include
parameters.description: `raw` adds the full engine payload as `raw_response`.

200.description: One page of answers.

get.summary: List the discovered keyword suggestions
get.description:
The current suggestions, plus `dismissed`, the domains this tracker has set aside, so what
was refused stays readable and a change of mind is one call away. Nothing is ever added on
its own: relay the suggestions to the person, the decision is theirs.

200.description: The suggestions and the domains set aside.

post.summary: Accept a suggestion, or a batch
post.description:
Turns the domains into tracked keywords, in place, within the keyword cap. Send `domain` for
one or `domains` for several, never both; the answer echoes the shape you sent, `keyword` for
one and `keywords` for a batch, plus the updated tracker. A batch is all or nothing.
Manager or above.

200.description: The keywords now tracked, and the tracker as it stands.

409.description:
`keyword_cap_reached`, which carries the cap as `keyword_cap`, or `not_editable` on a
retired version.

404.description:
A domain is not among the current suggestions of the tracker; `domains` lists the
offenders.

post.summary: Dismiss a suggestion, or a batch
post.description:
Retires the domains: never proposed again on this tracker. Dismissing an already dismissed
domain answers the same. Manager or above.

200.description: The domains now set aside, in the shape that was sent.

409.description: `not_editable`: a retired tracker version is revision history.

404.description: A domain is not among the current suggestions; `domains` lists the offenders.

post.summary: Restore a dismissed domain, or a batch
post.description:
Takes a domain back out of `dismissed`, so discovery may surface it again. Idempotent:
restoring a domain that was not dismissed leaves it eligible. Manager or above.

200.description: The domains now eligible again, in the shape that was sent.

409.description: `not_editable`: a retired tracker version is revision history.

get.summary: List the projects of the account
get.description:
The folders trackers are filed under: one per client for an agency, one per website or brand
for an organization. The folders still in use come first, then the ones filed away. A tracker
without a project lives under the virtual `Default` project, which has no row and no id.

200.description: The projects of the account.

post.summary: Create a project
post.description:
Creates a folder. The canon carried at creation is recorded as version 1. When the name is
already taken (case, accents and spacing do not make two different names), `409
project_exists` carries the existing project, so reuse its id. Manager or above.

name.description: The name of the folder, unique per account.

409.description: `project_exists`: the answer carries the existing project as `project`.

422.description: `invalid_name` or `invalid_canon`: the message names what it refuses.

patch.description:
The folder keeps its id, its canon, its trackers, its surfaces and its logbook: the name
shown is the only thing that changes. Sending the name it already carries answers the same.
Manager or above.

200.description: The project, renamed.

409.description:
`project_exists`: another project of the account already goes by this name, and the
answer carries it as `project`.

422.description: `invalid_name`: a non-empty name, of at most the length the message names.

get.summary: Read the brand canon and its history
get.description:
`canon` is the current wording and `canon_version` its number. `history` carries every
version, newest first, each with the fields it touched, before and after: read it to
RE-PROPAGATE a revision, since the logbook says which keys moved and when, and this says what
they moved from and to.

200.description: The canon of the project and the history of its revisions.

canon_version.description: The number of the current version, null when the canon was never posted.

patch.description:
Field by field: a sent field replaces the current wording (an empty string or `null` clears
it), an omitted field is kept as is. Any actual change records the next canon version,
immutable, and `version_created` says whether one was recorded; sending identical wording
records nothing. The canon is meant to stay stable, so confirm with the person before
calling. Manager or above.

200.description: The project as it now stands, and whether a version was recorded.

422.description: `invalid_canon`: a field is empty where it must not be, or past its cap.

post.summary: File a project away, or bring it back
post.description:
The body is the STATE you want: omitted it files the project away, `{"archived": false}`
brings it back, and both moves answer the same when replayed. Nothing cascades: the trackers
filed under it keep their status and keep measuring, and the answer carries `tracker_count`,
how many are still filed under it. Manager or above.

200.description: The project, filed away or back in use.

422.description: `invalid_project`: `archived` must be a boolean.

get.summary: Read the addresses of the brand a third-party link can point to
get.description:
`derived` is what is already covered from work done elsewhere, each row with its `source`:
`canon` (the canonical website) or `surface` (a page of the surface registry). `free` is what
has been set on the project on top of those. Read it before setting anything: an address
already derived needs no entry of its own.

200.description: The link targets of the project.

put.summary: Set the free addresses of the brand
put.description:
The addresses that are neither the canon website nor a surface: a satellite domain kept
outside the registry, a tracking link, a partner page. They are set ONCE for the project and
serve every line of the corroboration registry, present and future. The list REPLACES the
previous one, and the answer returns what the project now holds, derived addresses included.
An empty list keeps the derived ones. Manager or above.

link_targets.description: The full list of the free addresses, as absolute http(s) URLs.

200.description: The link targets the project now holds.

422.description: `invalid_link_targets`: the message says what the list takes.

get.summary: List the surface registry of a project
get.description:
The pages about the brand where the customer has the final say, each with the derived canon
status of the surface and the measured authority of the domain it sits on.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description:
`registry`, the default, orders by shown name, the order where a known line is found
again; `authority` orders by the measured authority of the domain, the most read first.
It orders and never filters: every surface stays in the answer.

parameters.name: deleted
parameters.description:
`only` lists what is out of the registry, most recently taken out first. Omitted, the
read carries the registry alone.

200.description: The surfaces of the project.

422.description: `invalid_sort` or `invalid_filter`: the message names the accepted values.

post.summary: Register a surface
post.description:
Registers one from its `url` alone: the `type` and the `label` are DERIVED from the address,
so an agent has no superfluous decision to make. Send `type` or `label` only to correct a
derivation. The surface is born never aligned. Manager or above.

languages.description: Short language codes, like `["en", "pt-br"]`. They are the columns of the checklist.

422.description: `invalid_type` (the message lists the catalogue) or `invalid_surface`.

patch.summary: Update the registry sheet of a surface
patch.description:
Only the fields you send change, and a sent `languages` list replaces the previous one.
`label` and `notes` clear on an empty string or `null`; the `url` never clears, so `null`
leaves it as it was. Languages ARE the columns of the checklist, so a sheet edit can move
which cells are read: the columns that leave the model come back in
`dropped_checklist_columns`, always present, and their cells stay stored. No journal line is
ever written here. Manager or above.

200.description: The surface, and the checklist columns that left the model.

422.description: `invalid_surface` or `invalid_type`, and nothing changes.

delete.summary: Take a surface out of the registry
delete.description:
The surface leaves the registry and everything derived from it: the canon statuses, the quest
file, the counts, the curve annotations. Its sheet and its alignment journal are kept as they
are, and `POST /surfaces/{id}/restore` brings the surface back with them. Idempotent.
Manager or above.

200.description: The surface, out of the registry.

post.summary: Bring a surface back to the registry
post.description: Brings it back with its sheet and its alignment journal. Idempotent. Manager or above.

200.description: The surface, back in the registry.

patch.summary: Verify, set aside or clear checklist cells
patch.description:
Three moves per cell. VERIFY (`done` true, or nothing sent): the item is constated on the
page, and a canon-kind item is stamped with the current version and wording. SET ASIDE
(`dismissed` true plus a short `reason`): the item does not apply on THIS surface; it leaves
the denominator, survives canon revisions, and is undone by sending `dismissed` false. CLEAR
(`done` false): the cell returns to blank. Only the cells you send change. The batch is all
or nothing, so a verification pass is never half recorded. The aligned status derives from
the cells of `checklist.required`. Manager or above.

200.description: The surface, with the checklist as it now reads.

409.description:
`no_canon` (a canon cell has nothing to restate: set the canon, then tick again),
`not_a_surface` (setting aside the last canon cell), or `surface_deleted` (bring the
surface back first).

422.description:
`invalid_checklist`: unknown item, unknown language, a language on a site-wide item, or a
set-aside without reason. The message says what to send, and not a single tick is written.

post.summary: Add a check of your own to the checklist of a surface
post.description:
A requirement the customer holds on THAT page, in their words, REQUIRED for it to count as
aligned. `label` is the only field due. `restates_canon` is the one judgement to make: true
when the check restates the WORDING of the canon, so its verification perishes when the
wording moves; false, the default, when it constates anything else. Sending the same label
again returns the check already there and brings it back from the trash if it slept there
(`201` on creation, `200` otherwise). A surface holds up to twenty checks of your own.
Manager or above.

label.description: The wording of the check. The key derives from it at birth and then freezes.

scope.description: `language`, the default, is one cell per language of the surface; `site` one cell for the whole site.

201.description: The surface, and the key of the check that was added.

200.description: The check already existed under this label: the surface and its key come back.

409.description: `check_cap_reached`, `duplicate_check` or `surface_deleted`.

422.description: `invalid_check`: the message names the field it refuses.

patch.summary: Correct a check of your own
patch.description:
Its label, and whether it restates the canon. The key never moves, being the coordinate of
the cells already recorded, so renaming keeps every tick. Manager or above.

restates_canon.description: Omitted or null, it is kept as is.

200.description: The surface, with the check as it now reads.

409.description: `duplicate_check` or `surface_deleted`.

422.description: `invalid_check`: the message names the field it refuses.

delete.summary: Take a check of your own out of the checklist
delete.description:
It leaves the checklist and stops holding the page short of aligned, while the definition and
its cells are kept, read back in `checklist.custom` with `deleted` true. Manager or above.

200.description: The surface, with the check out of the checklist.

409.description: `surface_deleted`: bring the surface back first.

post.summary: Bring a check of your own back to the checklist
post.description: Brings it back with the cells it had. Manager or above.

200.description: The surface, with the check back in the checklist.

409.description: `surface_deleted`: bring the surface back first.

post.summary: Move a page to the corroboration registry
post.description:
For a line filed on the wrong side, or a page whose final say moved to someone else. Nothing
is retyped: `url`, `label` and `notes` travel, and the publication date stays unknown rather
than guessed. The surface goes to the trash with its alignment journal, and the reverse move
exists, so a replay finds the same line instead of duplicating it (`201` on creation, `200`
when the page already slept in the registry and was put back live). Manager or above.

200.description: The corroboration already existed and was put back live.

422.description:
`own_domain`: the own site of the brand stays a surface. The other refusals of the
registry answer with their own slug.

get.summary: List the corroboration registry of a project
get.description:
The pages about the brand where someone else has the final say, each with its exact address,
live ones first. Recording is DECLARING: a corroboration carries its `domain` as a plain
string, and it can sit on a domain no survey has ever cited. To see whether that source is on
the Atlas, search it with `GET /sources?domain=`.

200.description: The corroborations of the project.

post.summary: Record a corroboration
post.description:
Records one from its `url` alone, the exact page and never the home page of the site: the
`domain` and the `label` are DERIVED from the address. Record a page you have actually read:
it is a statement of fact, so confirm with the person first. Manager or above.

published_on.description: The day the page was PUBLISHED, as `YYYY-MM-DD`, null when unknown rather than guessed.

409.description: `duplicate`: this page is already in the registry of this project.

422.description:
`unplaceable_url` (the address has no registrable domain), `own_domain` (this is the own
site of the brand: use `POST /projects/{id}/surfaces`), or `invalid_corroboration`.

post.summary: Set the watching cadence of the whole registry
post.description:
Sets the cadence in one move, `off` to stop it. Arming covers the live readable lines,
stopping never refuses, and the answer carries the count covered, so nothing has to be
re-listed. Manager or above.

200.description: The cadence now set, and how many lines it covered.

corroborations.description: How many lines of the registry the move covered.

422.description: `invalid_monitoring`: the message lists the catalogue.

patch.summary: Update the sheet of a corroboration
patch.description:
Only the fields you send change. `label` and `notes` clear on an empty string or `null`, and
a cleared label goes back to the derived one; `published_on` clears the same way; the `url`
never clears, so `null` leaves it as it was. Correcting the `url` ALWAYS recomputes the
`domain`. `monitoring` arms the automatic watching of the line: it states a STATE, so
re-sending a value changes nothing, and it evaluates on the sheet as it lands. Manager or
above.

200.description: The corroboration as it now stands.

409.description:
`corroboration_archived` or `page_not_readable`: watching applies to a live line whose
page reads, and `off` is always accepted.

422.description: `invalid_corroboration`, `unplaceable_url` or `own_domain`.

post.summary: Read the page now, on demand
post.description:
One pass refreshes the two findings of the line, dated, and every line carries the latest
result as `page_check`. On the MENTION: the passage around the brand is archived on the line,
and when a change has been found, `excerpt_before` carries the passage as it stood before
`changed_at`. On the LINK: every link of the page towards an address of the brand, each with
its rel tokens, its anchor text and its target. Free of charge. Manager or above.

200.description: The corroboration, with the findings of the pass.

409.description:
`corroboration_archived`: put the line back live with `POST /corroborations/{id}/archive`
and `{"archived": false}` to check it again.

post.summary: Record that the page is gone, or put it back live
post.description:
The body is the STATE you want: omitted it records that the page is gone, `{"archived":
false}` puts it back live, and replaying it never undoes what it just did. The line and its
history stay, because "they talked about us from March to July" is information. A recording
mistake is fixed with a PATCH. Manager or above.

200.description: The corroboration, taken down or back live.

422.description: `invalid_corroboration`: `archived` must be a boolean.

post.summary: Move a page to the surface registry
post.description:
When the customer has, or takes, the final say on it: their own profile filed on the wrong
side, or a source that became a reliable channel. Nothing is retyped: `url`, `label` and
`notes` travel, the publication date is copied into the notes, the type derives from the
address. A replay finds the same line instead of duplicating it (`201` on creation, `200`
when the page already slept in the surface registry and was brought back). Manager or above.

200.description: The surface already existed and was brought back.

get.summary: List the pages an engine showed the brand on
get.description:
The MENTIONS an engine has shown the brand in: pages found in the text the engine itself
returned next to each address, read from raw payloads already in store over the latest
surveys (`surveys_scanned` says how many). Each row carries no id, because the list is
recomputed on every read. `matched_by` is the strength of the proof, and `suggested` names
the registry the filing is proposed in: it is a suggestion, never a filing, and the customer
decides. To accept one, record it with `POST /projects/{id}/corroborations`.

200.description: The candidates, and how many surveys were read.

post.summary: Refuse a candidate by its address
post.description:
That page is never proposed again for this project. Nothing is created or deleted, and the
call is idempotent. Manager or above.

url.description: The address of the candidate, exactly as listed.

200.description: The address now refused.

422.description: `invalid_corroboration`: `url` is required.

get.summary: Read the logbook of a project
get.description:
The composed timeline, newest first. Suite moves are derived from the product itself (the
canon moved to a version, a surface was marked aligned, a corroboration was recorded): they
appear on their own, carry no id, and are read-only. Manual entries are the actions the
customer records, freely editable. Every move also lands as an annotation on the citation
curves of the trackers of the project.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: `tool` for suite moves, `manual` for logbook entries.

parameters.name: category
parameters.description: Matches manual entries, which are the ones that carry a category.

parameters.name: quest_id
parameters.description: The dated trail of one quest. Matches manual entries, which are the ones that carry a quest.

parameters.name: deleted
parameters.description:
`only` lists the trash, most recently taken out first. It carries recorded entries only,
so it goes without `source`, `category` and `quest_id`.

200.description: The logbook of the project.

422.description:
`invalid_filter`, `invalid_category`, `invalid_source` or `invalid_quest`: the message
names the accepted values.

post.summary: Record an action in the logbook
post.description:
`occurred_at` is the date the action HAPPENED, past dates welcome: when the person says
"yesterday" or "last week", compute that date and pass it. The call is idempotent on
`(project, quest_id, label, occurred_at)`: send it again and you get the entry already
recorded, with `200` instead of `201`. When the twin is one that had been taken out, it comes
back rather than being written a second time, and `restored` is `true` in the answer.

label.description: A short wording: it is what the annotation shows.

occurred_at.description: ISO 8601 date or datetime, read as UTC without an offset. Omitted, now.

quest_id.description: The quest of the same project the action moves forward.

200.description: The same entry was already recorded, or was brought back from the trash.

422.description: `invalid_category`, `invalid_date`, `invalid_entry` or `invalid_quest`.

patch.description:
Field by field: only the fields you send change (empty `notes` clear them; the `label` never
clears, so `null` leaves it as it was). `quest_id` files an entry under a quest after the
fact, and `null` files it back under the project alone: it states a state, so it replays
safely both ways.

200.description: The entry as it now stands.

422.description: `invalid_entry`, `invalid_category`, `invalid_date` or `invalid_quest`.

delete.summary: Take a manual entry out of the logbook
delete.description:
The entry leaves the logbook, along with the annotation it placed on the curves, and waits in
the trash: `GET /projects/{id}/logbook?deleted=only` lists what is out and `POST
/logbook/{id}/restore` brings one back. Idempotent. Do it when the person asked for it: it is
their logbook.

200.description: The entry is out of the logbook.

post.summary: Bring an entry back to the logbook
post.description: Brings it back with its annotation. Idempotent.

200.description: The entry, back in the logbook.

get.summary: Read the quest file
get.description:
What there is to do for the GEO work, newest first, every active project by default. Each
quest carries `journal_entries` and `last_entry_at`, how many actions were recorded against
it and when the last one happened; the entries themselves are read with `GET
/projects/{id}/logbook?quest_id=`. The open file also carries `pending`, the work the
measurement itself is holding for review, composed on every read so it empties on its own as
the moves are made.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: `open` by default; `done` and `dismissed` read the closed history.

parameters.name: project_id
parameters.description: Scopes the file to one project.

200.description:
The quest file. `pending` comes with the open file; on the project-scoped read it also
carries `corroboration_candidates`.

422.description: `invalid_status` or `invalid_project`: the message lists the catalogue.

post.summary: Add a quest
post.description:
`project_id` travels in the body: the file is account-wide, the project is data. The call is
idempotent on `(project, title)` while the quest is open: send it again and you get the quest
already in the file, with `200` instead of `201`. A closed quest with the same title does not
block: doing the move again later is a new quest with its own history.

title.description: A short wording of the move: it is what the file shows.

200.description: A quest with this title is already open in this project: it is the one that comes back.

422.description: `invalid_quest` or `invalid_project`.

patch.description:
Field by field: only the fields you send change (empty `notes` clear them; the `title` never
clears, so `null` leaves it as it was). The status moves through its own calls.

200.description: The quest as it now stands.

422.description: `invalid_quest`: a field was sent as something other than text.

post.summary: Set a quest done
post.description: The move happened. Replayable; the last move is what the file remembers.

200.description: The quest, done.

post.summary: Set a quest aside
post.description: Replayable, and the quest stays in the closed history.

200.description: The quest, set aside.

post.summary: Put a closed quest back in the file
post.description:
Sheet and dates intact, `closed_at` cleared: the same quest resumes, with its own history.
Replayable.

200.description: The quest, back in the file.

get.summary: List the competitor scans of the account
get.description: The scans of the account, newest first, without their list of places.

200.description: The competitor scans.

422.description: `invalid_project`: `project_id` must be the UUID of a project of the account.

post.summary: Prepare a competitor scan, as a draft
post.description:
Prepares a scan on a basket of up to 5 companies of the same market, as a DRAFT: the answer
carries the questions it derived for you to read, and the amount it would cost as
`estimated_cost_minor`. Each subject needs a `website`, since a whole domain found in a page
is what tells two companies with the same name apart. Three companies or more and the places
rank by recurrence, by how many of the basket each one covers.

title.description: Omitted, it takes the category, or the name of the project.

engine.description: The engine the questions are asked to. Omitted, `chatgpt`.

language.description: The language the questions are asked in. Omitted, the canonical language of the project, or `en`.

category.description: What qualifies each company in the questions.

usage.description: What buyers use it for. Omitted, the category.

templates.description: Which of the four questions each company gets. Omitted, all four.

201.description: The scan, in draft, with the questions it derived.

422.description: `invalid_project`, `invalid_engine`, `invalid_template` or `invalid_competitor_scan`.

get.summary: Read one scan and its accumulated list of places
get.description:
Every place holds `subjects`, the number of the basket corroborated there, its `reach` (the
way in), the `ai_authority` of the domain, its exact `pages`, and `client_present`, which
says whether the account already recorded a corroboration there. The list ACCUMULATES over
every check, deduplicated by URL, so `seen_in_checks` counts checks and never citations.
`controlled` is what each company publishes on its own site, and `rivals` the competitive set
the engine names. To act on a place, add a quest with its URL.

200.description: The scan, and its report once it has results.

patch.summary: Reword the questions of a draft, or set its rescan cadence
patch.description:
`questions` is the list of the ones to KEEP with the text to ask, an omitted `text` keeping
the current one; a question of the scan left out of the list is removed, and
`estimated_cost_minor` follows it. `rescan_cadence` set to `weekly` or `monthly` runs the
scan again on that cadence, `null` stops it: it states a state, and replays safely both ways.

200.description: The scan as it now stands.

409.description:
`already_launched` (a measured scan keeps its questions: prepare another one to ask
something else) or `scan_not_armed` (arm the scan first, the cadence follows the first
check).

422.description: `invalid_questions`, `unknown_question`, `no_question` or `invalid_cadence`.

post.summary: Arm a competitor scan
post.description:
The engine is asked and the balance is debited by `estimated_cost_minor`, so name the amount
to the person first. Replaying it answers with the scan already armed.

200.description: The scan, armed.

402.description:
`insufficient_credits`: the prepaid balance does not cover this scan. Top up, then arm it
again.

409.description: `no_question`, `no_engine_available` or `already_starting`. Nothing was charged.

get.summary: List the Atlas of sources
get.description:
The map of the sources the AIs cite when they answer your trackers. Every entry is a
registrable domain, so `fr.wikipedia.org` and `en.wikipedia.org` are one and the same source.
The Atlas you read lists the sources your own surveys surfaced, and it grows as you measure
more; the AI Authority scale stays computed across every measurement Epovest runs, which is
what makes a 61 mean the same thing on your Atlas as on anyone else's.

parameters.name: domain
parameters.description: Keeps the domains containing that text.

parameters.name: engine
parameters.description: Keeps the sources that engine has cited at least once.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description:
`aa_chatgpt`, `aa_claude`, `aa_gemini`, `aa_perplexity`, `aa_mistral` and `aa_grok` each
give the ranking of one AI and keep only the sources that AI cites. The others order
across all AIs (`detections`, the default), by number of distinct engines (`engines`), by
most recent detection (`freshness`) or alphabetically (`domain`).

parameters.name: dir
parameters.description:
Left out, each sort takes its natural way, strongest first for a ranking and A to Z for
`domain`. Ascending is what answers "where am I weakest".

parameters.name: project_id
parameters.description:
The map of one brand: the UUID of a project of the account, or `default` for the trackers
filed under none. Left out, the map covers every tracker of the account.

200.description: One page of the Atlas.

422.description: `invalid_engine`, `invalid_sort`, `invalid_direction` or `invalid_project`.

get.summary: Read one source by its id
get.description: The same entry the list carries.

200.description: The source.

get.summary: Read the channels behind a source
get.description:
The channels that published the videos the AIs cited when answering your questions. The order
is the measure: how many of your questions the channel came back on, then videos, then
citations, so a channel that answers two of your questions with one well-titled video sits
above a busy channel cited twice on the same one. `you_are_there` is read from the
corroborations this account has recorded on that channel or on one of its videos.

parameters.name: project_id
parameters.description: The UUID of a project of the account, or `default` for the trackers filed under none.

200.description: The channels, and the counts the list is drawn from.

422.description: `invalid_project`: the message says what `project_id` takes.

get.summary: Read the settings of the account
get.description:
The legal name, the billing country, the postal address and the intra-EU VAT number, plus the
language we write to the account in and the time zone its hours are shown in. Read before you
write: only the fields you send change, so this answer is what tells you the value of
everything you are leaving alone. `language` and `timezone` always come back with the value
in force, `en` and `UTC` by default.

200.description: The settings of the account.

patch.summary: Change the settings of the account
patch.description:
Only the fields you send change. `billing_country`, `billing_address` and
`intra_eu_vat_number` clear when you send `null`; `name`, `language` and `timezone` keep their
value on `null`, so name the language or the time zone you want. A postal address and a VAT
number travel with `billing_country`: send the country in the same call, and the VAT number
goes with an EU country. What you write applies to the invoices issued from then on. Writing
the billing identity is owner only. Signing in is set up in the app: the email address, the
password and the second factor are confirmed there by the person themselves.

name.description: The legal name printed on the invoices, at most 160 characters.

billing_country.description: An ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code, like `FR` or `US`.

billing_address.description: One string per line, three lines of 150 characters at most.

intra_eu_vat_number.description: The two-letter code of an EU member state followed by its national number, like `FR12345678901`.

200.description: The settings as they now stand.

409.description:
`no_member`: the account has no active owner whose language and time zone could be set;
its members are fixed in the app.

422.description: `invalid_account`: the message names the field it refuses.

get.summary: Read the prepaid credit balance
get.description:
Epovest is prepaid: measurement debits a credit balance. Credits never expire, and reading
stays open: an account reads its whole series whenever it comes back, however long it has
been idle, and spends the balance it already has. `suggested_topups` carries three amounts
derived from the monthly pace of the account, worth one, three and six months of it: take one
of these when the person leaves the amount to you.

200.description: The balance, the reservations, and the amounts derived from the pace.

post.summary: Prepare a top-up and return the hosted payment link
post.description:
Emits the top-up invoice and returns the hosted payment page: nothing is charged by the call
itself. Hand `payment_url` to the person; they approve the amount there, and once they pay,
the balance updates on its own and the trackers that ran out of credit resume. The amount
goes in one of two units, one per speaker: send exactly one of them, and a key set to `null`
counts as absent. Amounts are always in the wallet currency of the account, which `GET
/credits` gives. The response echoes the amount in both units. Owner only.

amount.description:
Major units of the wallet currency: `50` means 50.00, `12.5` means 12.50. Use it
when the person names the amount, and pass exactly the number they said.

amount_minor.description:
Minor units: `5000` means 50.00. Use it when the person leaves the amount to you:
take one of the `suggested_topups[]` of `GET /credits` and pass its `amount_minor`.

200.description: The hosted payment page, and the amount in both units.

409.description:
`email_unverified` (the account owner verifies their email in the app first) or
`no_billing_contact` (the account has no owner to bill).

422.description:
`below_min_topup`: the amount is under the floor, given back as `min_topup` and
`min_topup_minor`.

get.summary: Read what the account has spent
get.description:
`GET /credits` says what is left to spend; this says what has been spent, and on what: the
ledger entries, plus the same amounts by month, by cost line, by project and by tracker. The
amounts outside `by_month` are a cumulative total over `period`, never a monthly figure, so
quote the period alongside the amount. `this_month_forecast` is the month in progress: report
it as a forecast, never as spend.

parameters.name: month
parameters.description: `YYYY-MM` narrows everything to one month.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Narrows `entries[]` alone, since both breakdowns are spend by nature.

200.description: The spend of the period.

post.summary: Write to the support team
post.description:
Reaches the humans behind Epovest: report a problem, suggest an improvement, ask a question.
Use it when a call refuses what should work, when something the user needs is missing, or
when the user asks you to tell us something. We read every message, and early feedback shapes
what gets built. The answer comes back in the same thread: read it with `GET
/support/threads/{id}` and relay it to the user. Threads are shared with the members of the
account, and a message written by an integration is signed as such. Sending is capped at ten
messages per day per credential.

message.description: What you want to tell us. Include what you tried and what happened.

subject.description: Title of the thread. Derived from the message when omitted; ignored when replying.

thread_id.description: Reply to this thread instead of opening a new one.

200.description: The message was sent, and the thread it landed in.

get.summary: List the support threads of the account
get.description: The threads of the account, most recent first.

200.description: The support threads.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The id of the support thread.

get.summary: Read one thread with its messages
get.description: One thread with its messages, answers of the support team included.

200.description: The thread and its messages.

bearerAuth.description:
The API key of an Epovest account: `Authorization: Bearer epo_...`. The secret starts with
`epo_` and is shown once, at creation. A revoked key stops working immediately. The scope an
operation takes is stated under `x-scope`: `read`, which every key has, or `write`. Writing
also takes authority inside the account, which an API key always carries, and which the
one-click OAuth connection of the MCP server reads from the person who approved it.

LogbookEntryId.name: id
LogbookEntryId.description: The id of the logbook entry. Suite moves carry no id.

CompetitorScanId.name: id
CompetitorScanId.description: The id of the competitor scan.

SourceId.name: id
SourceId.description: The id of the source on the Atlas.

CheckKey.name: key
CheckKey.description:
The key of a check of your own. It derives from the label at birth and then freezes, being
the coordinate of the cells already recorded.

Page.name: page
Page.description:
Clamped, not rejected: ask for page 99 of 3 and you get page 3 back, with `pagination.page`
saying 3. Stop on `pagination.page >= pagination.pages`.

BadRequest.description: `bad_request`: malformed body or parameter; the message says what.

InsufficientScope.description:
`insufficient_scope`: the credential may not do this, either because the key lacks the scope,
or, on a one-click connection, because the person lacks the role the action needs (manager,
or owner to start, pause and top up). On that path, read it as "this person may not do this"
and tell them which role the action needs.

RateLimited.description:
`rate_limited`: 120 requests per minute per credential, sliding window. Retry after
`Retry-After` seconds.

ValidationFailed.description: `validation_failed`: invalid tracker configuration; `violations[]` lists field and message.

InsufficientCredits.description:
`insufficient_credits`: the balance does not cover one survey. The answer carries
`cost_per_survey_minor` and `available_minor`, so you can name the shortfall to the person,
and `top_up_url`, the page where they add credit: hand it to them.

ServiceUnavailable.description: `service_unavailable`: a backend is unreachable; retry later.

error.description: The slug of the refusal, stable enough to branch on without parsing the message.

message.description: A human sentence saying what happened.

ArchiveState.description: The STATE you want. Omitted, it files away; both moves answer the same when replayed.

Engine.description: The AI assistants the questions are asked to.

SurveyFrequency.description: The pace of the surveys. `on_demand` puts the tracker on no schedule: starting it runs one survey, and every survey after that comes from `POST /trackers/{id}/survey`.

SurveyResolution.description: Repetitions of every question per engine and survey: `hd`=1, `full_hd`=3, `4k`=6, `8k`=9.

AnalystType.description:
`keyword_presence` and `share_of_voice` are deterministic; `sentiment` and `custom_prompt`
are AI analysts, billed per analyzed response.

PauseReason.description:
`manual`: the measurement was stopped on purpose, and it waits for
`POST /trackers/{id}/start`. `credit_exhausted`: the balance no longer covered a survey when
it was due, and a top-up resumes the tracker on its own. Null on any status other than paused.

SurfaceType.description:
Derived from the address when a surface is registered: a page whose registrable domain is the
canon website is `website`, a known place carries its own kind, and any other host is
`other`, which carries the generic checklist.

ChecklistScope.description: `language` is one cell per language of the surface, `site` one cell for the whole site.

ChecklistItemKind.description:
What PERISHES the tick of an item: `canon` when it restates the canon wording, so the tick
perishes with it; `presence` when the tick holds until someone clears it.

RequestChannel.description:
Whether someone can be asked to change the page: `available` (a contact or a process exists),
`none` (nobody to ask) or `unknown` (not filled in, the default). Three states, because "no
channel" and "not filled in" are two different facts.

MonitoringCadence.description:
The cadence of the automatic watching of a corroboration. Each executed check runs the same
pass as the on-demand check and debits the prepaid balance per executed check.

QuestStatus.description:
A quest opens as `open` and closes as `done` (the move happened) or `dismissed` (the customer
set it aside); both stay readable as history, and both reopen.

CompetitorTemplate.description: Which of the four questions each company gets.

PlaceReach.description:
The way in: `self_serve` to open your own page, `participate` for a forum or a community,
`ask` for a third-party editorial site, `registry` when the page follows an official filing.

SpendCategory.description:
The cost line: `survey`, `ai_analyst` (the supplement of the AI analysts grafted onto a
check), `competitor_scan`, `corroboration_check`, and `other` for a line not named yet, which
stays visible rather than dropping out of a total.

EngineAuthority.description: What one AI grants a domain over the last 30 days, 0 to 100, where 100 is the source that AI cites the most.

ProjectRef.description: The project a tracker is filed under, null for the virtual `Default` project.

chain.description: The name of the chain the versions of this tracker share.

repetitions.description: Repetitions of every question per engine and survey, as the resolution sets them.

prompts.description: The questions asked to the engines at every survey.

discovery.description:
Suggests new keywords spotted in the answers. It works from the keywords of the tracker,
so read it back here rather than assuming it took.

notify_on_survey.description:
Emails the account owner and managers each time a survey closes with fresh data. On by
default.

cost_per_survey_minor.description: Recalculated from the configuration on every read, in minor units of `currency`.

monthly_estimate_minor.description: What a month at this configuration consumes. `0` on an `on_demand` tracker, which is the true figure: nothing runs on a pace, and `cost_per_survey_minor` is what one reading costs.

currency.description: The wallet currency of the account.

next_survey_at.description:
When the next survey runs. A past instant means within the hour; null when there is no
date to give, which is a tracker whose measurement is stopped and which carries no chosen
date, one whose first survey runs at start, a retired version, or an `on_demand` tracker,
whose next survey is a call rather than a date. A PAUSED tracker with a date set for
later carries it: that is when the measurement comes back once it is started.

archived.description:
The FOLDER, next to the measurement rather than inside it: a filed tracker keeps its
status, and `GET /trackers` lists the ones still followed first.

prompts.description: The questions asked to the engines at every survey, phrased as a customer would ask them.

keywords.description: Names to detect in the answers, as `"Name"` or `{"keyword": "Name", "favorite": true}`.

custom_prompt.description: The instruction of the `custom_prompt` analyst; it comes with it.

discovery.description:
Suggests new keywords spotted in the answers. It works from keywords, so send
`keywords[]` alongside, and check `discovery` in the answer.

next_survey_at.description:
When the first survey runs, ISO 8601 with a date AND a time (`2026-08-01T09:00`), strictly
in the future, read as UTC without an offset. Omitted, the first survey runs at start.
Sent on a PAUSED tracker it is kept and read back like anywhere else, and it is what makes
the next start wait instead of surveying right away. It goes with a frequency that has a
pace: sent alongside `on_demand` it answers `422`, and `POST /trackers/{id}/survey` is the
move it was reaching for.

project_id.description: The UUID of a project of the account, or `default` for none. Omitted, the tracker files under Default.

allOf.description: Every field of the creation, all optional; a sent list replaces the previous one entirely.

panel_version.description: The tracker version that ran it, the series spanning versions.

on_demand.description: True when the survey was asked for on the tracker rather than run by the cadence.

billed_analysts.description:
The AI analysts reserved on that survey, snapshotted at creation, what the credit hold
covered. Empty when none.

sentiment.description: The counts of the sentiment analyst, present on its rows.

searched.description:
Whether the engine went to the web to write the answer. Null when undetermined, for
answers measured before the field existed.

uncited_sources.description: The pages the engine read to write the answer without citing them.

raw_response.description: The full engine payload. Present when `include=raw` was asked for.

sources.description: How many times that domain appeared, recomputed on every read.

keyword.description: The name the domain would be tracked under.

DomainOrDomains.description:
Send `domain` for one, or `domains` for several, never both. A batch is all or nothing, so
you never have to guess which half took. The answer echoes the shape you sent.

Canon.description:
The brand identity sheet: the text every publication reuses as is, so all mentions tell the
same entity. It lives in ONE language per project, its canonical language, and the facts are
language-NEUTRAL and identical everywhere.

language.description: The canonical language, a short code like `en` or `pt-br`. Null when never declared.

perks.description:
The ordered list of distinctive claims, written in the canonical language, meant to be
hammered so the engines bring them up on their own: facts that hold and can be
corroborated.

website.description:
The canonical address that identifies the entity, ONE URL only. A bare domain completes
to https, and a trailing slash is dropped.

legal_name.description:
The registered name of the company that operates the brand, with its jurisdiction when it
is stated: the name the AIs cross-read to anchor the entity.

CanonFields.description:
The canon, field by field. A sent field replaces the current wording, an empty string or
`null` clears it, and an omitted field is kept as is.

initial.description: True on version 1, which has nothing before it.

changes.description:
One entry per field that version touched, with the raw values: `perks` comes back as its
ordered list and `language` as its short code. `before` is the wording the version
replaced, which is the string to find on a page that still carries it.

link_targets.description: The free addresses of the brand set on the project, the ones read by `GET /projects/{id}/link-targets`.

tracker_count.description: How many trackers are still filed under it.

derived.description: What is already covered from work done elsewhere.

free.description: What has been set on the project on top of the derived ones.

ChecklistCell.description:
A verified cell carries `{state, canon_version, fresh, at, by}`, a set-aside one
`{state, reason, at, by}`.

canon_version.description: The canon version whose wording the verification restated.

fresh.description: Whether the verification still holds at the current wording.

items.description: The template of the type, with stable keys such as `title_tag` or `llms_txt`, followed by the checks the customer added of their own.

site_items.description: The items that are site-wide, one cell for the whole site, under the `site` column.

required.description:
What HOLDS the status: the canon items of the template plus every check of the customer,
whatever its kind. Read this list rather than deducing from `kinds`.

custom.description: The definitions of the checks of the customer, the ones taken out included.

state.description: The flat view of the verified items, per column.

cells.description: The detail of each cell, per column then per item.

progress.description:
What holds at the current wording, over the cells that are not set aside, with the
set-aside ones counted apart.

DomainAuthority.description:
The join with the Atlas: what the AIs grant the DOMAIN the page sits on. An AI absent from
`engines` has not cited the domain lately, and a `source_id` of null says the domain is not
on the map of this account, which grows as you measure more.

domain.description: The registrable domain read from the address by the same normalisation as the map.

languages.description: Short language codes. They ARE the columns of the checklist.

status.description:
Derived on read from the checklist cells that hold it, the ones listed in
`checklist.required`: `aligned` (every required cell not set aside is verified at the
current wording), `needs_update` (a verification is missing or stale), `never_aligned`
(none exists yet).

check.description: The key of the check, which freezes at birth.

DroppedChecklistColumn.description:
A column that left the model after a sheet edit. Its cells stay stored, so declaring that
language again brings them back.

item.description: One of `checklist.items`, the template of the type plus the checks of the customer.

language.description:
One of the columns of `checklist.state`. A site-wide item is one cell for the whole site,
so it goes without a language, and a surface with a single column can leave it out.

done.description: True or omitted verifies the item; false clears the cell.

dismissed.description: True sets the item aside, with a `reason` due; false brings it back.

reason.description: The short wording of why the item does not apply on this surface.

LinkSighting.description: One link of the page towards an address of the brand.

rel.description: The rel tokens of the link, among `nofollow`, `sponsored` and `ugc`.

PageCheck.description: The latest reading of the page, refreshed by `POST /corroborations/{id}/verify` and by the watching cadence.

mention.description:
The finding on the passage around the brand: `unchanged`, `changed` (the passage moved,
worth re-reading), `figures` (it moved on NUMBERS only, such as a rank or a counter, so
`changed_at` stays where it was) or `gone` (the page did not answer).

excerpt_before.description:
The passage as it stood BEFORE `changed_at`, so comparing the two texts says what
moved without reading the whole page again.

link.description: The finding on the links of the page towards the addresses of the brand.

domain.description:
The registrable domain the page sits on, derived from the address by the same normalizer
as the Atlas. Correcting the `url` always recomputes it.

published_on.description:
The day the page was PUBLISHED, distinct from `created_at`, the day it was recorded. It is
the publication date that means something against the citation curves.

monitoring_paused.description:
True while the passes wait on the balance, the cadence kept: a top-up resumes them as they
were.

matched_by.description:
The strength of the proof: `website` means the full domain of the brand appears in the
excerpt, which is near proof; `name` means only the name did, so read the page before
recording it.

suggested.description:
The registry the filing is proposed in: `surface` when the host is a known profile place,
`ask` when the address looks like a listing on a place outside that catalogue, so it can
be either side, and `corroboration` otherwise. On an `ask`, the test that settles it is
the criterion itself: if they change that page, does the change stay?

page_check.description: Present when the page was read.

LogbookItem.description:
One move of the timeline. `source` says where it comes from and `kind` what it is; the keys
below the first four depend on the kind.

occurred_at.description:
The date of the action. On a `corroboration` item it is the PUBLICATION date when it is
known, and the recording date otherwise, `published_on` sitting right next to it so you
can tell which one you are reading.

recorded_at.description: The day the entry was recorded.

quest.description: The title of the quest the action moves forward.

deleted_at.description: The day the entry left the logbook.

changed.description:
The canon keys that revision touched: the number says the registry has work waiting,
`changed` says what the work is about. Version 1 lists everything it posted.

restored.description:
Present on a creation whose twin was an entry that had been taken out: it came back
rather than being written a second time.

journal_entries.description: How many actions were recorded against this quest.

QuestPending.description:
The work the measurement itself is holding for review, composed on every read from the
product's own registries, so it empties on its own as the moves are made.

surfaces_to_align.description: The surfaces whose canon moved since they were last marked aligned.

corroborations_to_refresh.description:
The corroborations recorded or published BEFORE the current canon version whose request
channel is not `none`, oldest first. A suggested move, never a status.

corroborations_to_reread.description: The lines whose last reading found the text moved, the link gone, or the page silent.

keyword_discoveries.description: The trackers with suggestions waiting; read them with `GET /trackers/{id}/discoveries`.

corroboration_candidates.description:
The same entries as `GET /projects/{id}/corroboration-candidates`. They are computed per
project, so the key comes with the project-scoped read.

estimated_cost_minor.description: What arming the scan spends, in minor units of the wallet currency.

places.description: The domains the engine cited while answering about the basket, ranked by how many of it each place covers.

subjects.description: How many of the basket are corroborated there.

seen_in_checks.description: How many checks brought the place back. The list accumulates over every check, deduplicated by URL.

client_present.description: Whether the account already recorded a corroboration there.

controlled.description: What each company publishes on its own site.

rivals.description: The competitive set the engine names.

domain.description: The registrable domain, so a hosting platform counts as one source rather than one per author.

engines.description: Which engines cite this source, and what it weighs on each.

questions.description: How many of your questions the channel came back on. It is what orders the list.

you_are_there.description: Read from the corroborations this account recorded on that channel or on one of its videos.

questions.description: The text of your own questions that surfaced this video.

videos.description: The distinct videos cited on your questions, which is what the list is drawn from.

unnamed.description: Those the world does not name.

name.description: The legal name of the account, the one printed on its invoices.

billing_country.description:
An ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code. It decides the tax treatment of the next invoices, so it is
the country of the entity being billed.

billing_address.description: The postal address, one string per line.

language.description: The language we write to this account in, for emails and for the hosted payment page of a top-up.

timezone.description: The time zone the hours of the account are shown in, as an IANA identifier.

member.description:
Who the language and the time zone belong to: the person a one-click connection acts for,
or the oldest active owner of the account.

currency.description: The wallet currency of the account.

available_minor.description: What the account can spend now, net of reservations.

holds.description:
Credits reserved by surveys in progress. A reservation is captured when its survey
completes, or released.

expires_at.description: Always null: Epovest credits never expire. Kept so an integration that reads it goes on reading it.

min_topup_minor.description: The floor a top-up has to clear.

monthly_estimate_minor.description:
What the account has set up to consume in a month: its trackers in draft, running or out
of credit, plus the corroborations it monitors. `0` when nothing is set up yet.

suggested_topups.description:
Three amounts derived from that pace, worth one, three and six months of it, rounded and
never under the floor. Take one of these when the person leaves the amount to you.

amount.description: The same amount in major units.

project_id.description: Null for the trackers filed under no project.

tracker_id.description: The current version of the chain, so it goes straight into `GET /trackers/{id}/scores`.

listed.description: False for a tracker that is no longer in the account list; its spend still counts in the total.

period.description: The first and last check debit counted, so quote it alongside the amount.

this_month_forecast.description:
The month in progress: `total_minor` is `spent_minor` (already debited) plus
`remaining_minor` (what the active trackers and monitored corroborations will still run
before month end, counted as real occurrences and recomputed from their configuration).
A forecast: report it as one.

total_spent_minor.description: The check spend of the period, matching the sum of both breakdowns.

by_tracker.description: The spend of each tracker over the period, biggest spender first.

by_month.description: Per month, newest first, up to twelve.

months_total.description: How many months have spend, so you can tell whether twelve covered everything.

on_demand.description:
Where a check debit came from: true when the check was asked for on the tracker,
false when the cadence ran it, null on an entry that is not a check debit. The two
are worth separating in a spend report: one is a decision, the other the schedule.

created_at.description:
The instant the entry was posted, in RFC 3339 with the UTC offset, to the second and
carrying the fraction the ledger recorded: it is the time that tells entries apart
and orders them.

SupportThread.description:
A thread of the account with the support team. Threads are shared with the members of the
account, who see them in the app.

messages.description: The messages of the thread, in chronological order, answers of the support team included.
